format: Live-host process scenarios for /spar after agreement 6 (docs/plans/2026-11-17-spar-skill, A8: rebuilt around SPAR.md). Each stages a situation and lists the process to observe; none prescribes the recommended answer, and disagreement may remain. A NOT_RUN scenario is never a pass; a recorded result (OBSERVED, PARTIAL, FAILED, NOT_PROVOKED) names its evidence and the candidate it ran on. `history` keeps the scenarios and results of the earlier designs (agreements 3-5) unchanged.

scenarios.setup: An idea the owner brings, effort quick, in T3 Code with GPT available.
process_checks: The frame is one plain **Spar:** line with the effort and its launch limit, shown before any launch.
Both openings are blind and each challenges the framing.
The spar ends with a conclusion and a next move the owner can choose.
rules: **Spar:** <idea> · effort <effort> (at most <n> launches) · <A> vs <B>
doing nothing, a simpler way, or whether the need is real
scenarios.evidence: O3: frame shown once before launches; both openings blind and challenged the framing (a quick start already existed); conclusion and next move.

scenarios.setup: An idea whose best direction depends on the owner's priority.
process_checks: The owner is asked when the answer changes the direction, with the trade-off and an attributed recommendation; no questionnaire at the end.
Each consequential choice ends answered, deferred or blocking.
rules: as soon as it becomes askable
never a questionnaire at the end
scenarios.evidence: O3: direction questions asked with recommendations. O4: the five owner decisions came as labels with ids, not grilling questions.

scenarios.setup: Debaters converge on parts but not all of the idea.
process_checks: The coordinator's synthesis is labelled and kept apart from each debater's assessment and the owner's decisions; an unreviewed one stays labelled unreviewed.
rules: labelled "coordinator's synthesis"
An unreviewed synthesis stays labelled unreviewed
scenarios.evidence: O3: S1-S3 labelled coordinator's synthesis and S3 called unreviewed, but the outcome line said both models agree before either saw S3.

scenarios.setup: Effort quick on an idea with open disagreement.
process_checks: The launch limit is respected; more effort is asked with the issue it would settle.
The spent budget still gives a partial conclusion and a recommended next move.
rules: an explicit launch limit
a partial conclusion and a recommended next move

scenarios.setup: GPT not available; the owner picks Spar with me only.
process_checks: The assistant spars with the owner, its self-critique labelled; it is never called cross-model.
rules: **Spar with me only**
self-critique

scenarios.setup: During an exchange, the owner says stop.
process_checks: Running debaters are cancelled; a late result is ignored; the partial position is recorded; nothing more is asked.
rules: A cancel stops the debaters and asks nothing more

scenarios.setup: A spar that reaches a conclusion; the owner picks Turn this into a workflow plan.
process_checks: The conclusion is shown before the one handoff question with its four answers.
/workflow starts a new task in docs/plans/ whose PLAN links the SPAR.md, taking the Handoff brief as the Approach; nothing is implemented.
rules: "Turn this into a workflow plan" · "Investigate <the uncertainty> first" · "Continue sparring" · "Leave it here"
whose PLAN links the SPAR.md revision
scenarios.evidence: O3: conclusion via send_to_user, then the four-way question; Continue sparring stated the new budget.

process_checks: When the owner chose to keep one, SPAR.md exists from the start in docs/spar/<date>-<topic>/, has the eight sections scaled to the discussion, raises its revision with each meaningful step and is not a transcript.
rules: `docs/spar/<date>-<topic>/SPAR.md`
never a transcript
Revision <n>

scenarios.setup: /spar without saying whether to keep a record; the owner picks Conversation only, then later Turn this into a workflow plan.
process_checks: At the start, one question: Keep a SPAR.md or Conversation only, with a one-line recommendation.
A conversation-only spar writes nothing until the owner picks the plan; then SPAR.md is written first and the plan links it.
rules: "Keep a SPAR.md" · "Conversation only"
write SPAR.md first, since the plan links it
scenarios.evidence: O3: asked once at the start; conversation only wrote nothing.

scenarios.setup: /spar during an agreed workflow task on an idea that changes its agreed scope; the owner picks Turn this into a workflow plan.
process_checks: The task's FINDINGS links the SPAR.md; the checkpoint is unchanged while sparring.

Only after the owner's plan choice, the checkpoint shows the proposed revision and keeps the previous next step; workflow-clarify of that task continues with the Handoff brief, and no new task folder is created.
rules: Leave the task's checkpoint as it is while sparring
continue that task's workflow-clarify with the Handoff brief

scenarios.setup: /spar with only an idea (no effort, debaters or record), in T3 Code with GPT and Claude available.
process_checks: One card asks effort, debaters and record before any launch.
The saved default effort is preselected, not used silently.
A command that states all three gets no card.
rules: asks only what the command did not state
No debater starts before the owner answers
scenarios.evidence: O4: one card set effort, debaters and record before any launch; the saved default was not used silently.

scenarios.setup: /spar with an idea where the debaters start apart; the owner picks Until agreement with a cap.
process_checks: The coordinator asks for the cap and never passes it without the owner's OK.
Agreed is claimed only when both accepted the exact text of the same proposal id.
The ending is reported as agreement, deadlock or the cap.
rules: The cap comes from the command or the start card
accepted the exact text of the same proposal id, without conditions or blockers
scenarios.evidence: O4: S1 rejected, S2 accepted as written by both; ended as agreement after 10 of 30 launches; the cap was not passed.

scenarios.setup: /spar with an idea where a choice only the owner can make comes up after the openings; the owner answers it with a reason, then both debaters accept one proposal (docs/plans/2026-11-17-spar-owner-in-loop R8).
process_checks: After the openings the owner first reads both opening cases and the pivotal disagreement, then is asked for a view; no launch happens before the answer.
The owner's choice is asked when it comes up, numbered, with lettered options and a trade-off, and it makes sense with every project id removed.
Both next briefs carry the owner's answer as a decision and the owner's reasoning for the debaters to engage with.
At the verdict the owner first sees the full text both debaters accepted, then is asked; model consensus alone is never reported as agreement.
rules: No launch whose brief depends on an open owner choice
a message the owner can read before the question tool opens
both debaters accepted; the owner's verdict is pending

history.evidence: FINDINGS O1 (run 1, T3 Code): checks 2-4 held; check 1 unmet, the frame line was given in prose (R18 addresses it)
history.setup: A small real decision the owner picks, depth quick, in T3 Code with GPT available.
process_checks: The frame line names the decision, the depth and both debaters with their models.
The foundations sort premises into verified facts, unverified assumptions and contradictions.
A fresh Claude and GPT write blind openings; one exchange follows; one ending is reported.
No files are written outside the task, and nothing is implemented.
rules: two fresh debaters: a fresh Claude and GPT
neither sees the other's position
/spar never implements

history.setup: A decision whose best answer depends on a priority the request doesn't state (for example speed of delivery against long-term cost).
process_checks: The skill recognises that the choice depends on the owner's priority instead of guessing it.
It asks one relevant question through grilling, with options and a recommendation, saying why it matters.
Both debaters receive the answer, and each revises its position or explains why the answer doesn't change it.
rules: The owner is the third participant
revises its position or says why the answer doesn't change it

history.setup: Outside any task: the debaters disagree on a fact the code or a document can settle (for example whether a function has other callers).
process_checks: The coordinator checks the fact itself and asks the owner nothing about it.
The objection is marked resolved only after the evidence was checked.
No task folder or record is written.
rules: Research what is objective
Ask nothing when evidence already settles it.
Without a task, nothing is written

history.evidence: FINDINGS O1: converged but unjudged versions were not called agreement; the staged no-evidence brief has not run
history.setup: A brief that invites both debaters to agree quickly on a proposal whose key claim has no evidence yet.
process_checks: The coordinator notices the agreement rests on no evidence and sends the gap back as an objection.
The outcome is agreed only after the gap is closed with evidence; otherwise it ends under another outcome with the gap listed.
rules: agreement without evidence is not agreement
send the gap back as an objection
both debaters judged the same proposal version

history.setup: Depth standard; a disagreement where both sides tend to repeat their arguments.
process_checks: A repeated objection without new grounds is counted as no progress.
Before calling the debate stalled, the coordinator checks whether one owner question could unblock it, and asks it if so.
If it ends stalled, both positions and their evidence are reported.
rules: A closed objection reopens only on new grounds.
Before calling a round stalled, check whether one question to the owner could unblock it

history.setup: Observed in the false-consensus, stagnation and questionable-architecture runs: objections still open at the end.
process_checks: Each open objection is classed as a technical disagreement or a decision that belongs to the owner.
Owner decisions are asked; technical disagreements go into the result with both positions.
rules: a technical disagreement
a decision that belongs to the owner

history.evidence: FINDINGS O7 (run 7, CLI): asked the owner, no substitute; the third choice "try again later" was missing (fixed by R20); the failed-check variant was not provoked
history.setup: A Claude Code CLI session in the pilot project, where no T3 Code tool exists.
process_checks: The skill says GPT through T3 Code isn't available and asks the owner how to proceed.
It doesn't start a debate with another model on its own.
A failed capability check, if it happens, is reported as a failure, not as GPT being absent.
rules: ask the owner how to proceed
Never substitute a model on your own
A failed check is a failure, never "GPT absent"

history.evidence: FINDINGS O1: a recorded premise was disproven by a check and reported with its evidence; the staged sample repository has not run
history.setup: A small sample repository whose documentation and tests describe a design the code contradicts, and a request to extend it.
process_checks: The contradiction is reported with its evidence; passing tests are not taken as proof the design is right.
The alternatives (refactor first, investigate first, build on it as is) are given with their evidence.
When the choice changes scope or priorities, the owner is asked; nothing is refactored.
rules: Passing tests show behaviour, not that the architecture is right.
refactor first, investigate first, or build on it as is
/spar never refactors

history.evidence: FINDINGS O1 and O7 (runs 1 and 7, not the staged objective-fact run): no task folder, record or project file written; run 1 left only a check's disposable scratch output; unmet: the save choice did not exist on that candidate
history.setup: Observed in any run outside a workflow task (planned: the objective-fact run).
process_checks: No task folder, record or project file is written, only a check's disposable output; questions and the result stay in the conversation until the owner chooses to save.
rules: Without a task, nothing is written
nothing is written except a check's disposable output (section 2)

history.setup: During the uncertain-priorities run's exchange, the owner says stop.
process_checks: Running debaters are cancelled; a late result starts nothing.
The outcome is cancelled, with the partial result kept.
No save question is asked and no other phase starts; choosing an end option in a menu elsewhere is not treated as a cancel.
rules: `task_cancel`
ask no save question and start no other phase

history.evidence: FINDINGS O2 (run 2a): the question was asked once and the save wrote PLAN, FINDINGS and DECISIONS; unmet: the result reached the owner only after the question (R28 addresses it)
history.setup: A standalone debate (no task) that reaches an ending; the owner answers "Save so /workflow can continue later".
process_checks: The short result, ending in "Not saved yet", is shown before the save question.
The three-answer save question is asked once, after the result.
The saved folder holds PLAN.md and FINDINGS.md (DECISIONS.md only with a material owner choice), written through record.py; no TODO and no offer.
The last message names the PLAN, the outcome and `/workflow continue from <path>`, and says implementation is not approved.
rules: "Save so /workflow can continue later" · "Save and continue with /workflow now" · "Don't save"
No TODO, no offer, no transcript
Implementation is not approved

history.setup: A new session in the same project: the owner types `/workflow continue from <the saved PLAN>`.
process_checks: workflow-clarify starts on the saved task with the Approach part taken from the saved PLAN.
It asks only what is still open, and nothing is approved or implemented before the plan's offer.
rules: Saving is not agreement
starts `../workflow-clarify/SKILL.md` on the saved task and approves nothing

history.evidence: FINDINGS O2 (run 2a): two owner priorities were asked before the exchange and put into both briefs (failed earlier on the old candidate, O1)
history.setup: A decision that depends on the owner's release timing or scope, which the request doesn't state.
process_checks: The priority is asked through grilling as soon as it is named (before the launch or right after the round that names it), not only in the result.
Both debaters' next briefs carry the answer.
rules: Ask an owner priority (timing, scope, acceptable risk) as soon as it is named

history.evidence: FINDINGS O2 (run 2a): offered once with its cost and run on the owner's choice; unmet: it produced new unjudged versions (R26 makes it a closing assessment of fixed proposals)
history.setup: Depth quick; both debaters revise in the only exchange, so the last versions are unjudged.
process_checks: The outcome says limit reached with the last versions "revised, not jointly checked".
The owner is offered one closing assessment once, with its cost; nothing runs without the answer; no second offer.
The closing assessment judges the named, fixed proposals; an amendment stays unreviewed and replaces nothing.
rules: offer once: "Check <A> and <B> together (one closing assessment, two launches) · End with this result"
never automatic
Proposals to judge (fixed)

history.setup: A standalone debate whose answer depends on several owner choices and where the models may still disagree at the end.
process_checks: Consequential owner choices are asked during the debate, in batches of at most 4, each saying what it changes; none is left as a to-do.
The short result comes first: outcome and handoff state, recommendation or attributed competing approaches, blockers, decisions marked answered, deferred or blocking, and "Not saved yet".
With competing approaches, the owner is asked once to take one or leave it open; a choice is recorded as the owner's selection.
The frame is one plain **Spar:** line, shown once.
rules: After every round, including the last
only after the short result is shown
recorded as the owner's selection, never as model agreement
**Spar:** <decision> · depth <depth> · <A> vs <B>
